Dear Chairman Mendelson:
Pursuant to section 451 of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act (D.C. Official Code § 1 -
204.51) and section 202 of the Procurement Practices Reform Act of 2010 (D.C. Official Code §
2-352.02), enclosed for consideration and approval by the Council of the District of Columbia is a
proposed resolution, the “Contract No. DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C PPA-26-01 with Flywheel
Development, LLC Emergency Approval Resolution of 2026”, and accompanying emergency
declaration resolution.
Under the proposed definitive contract, Flywheel Development, LLC will develop solar
photovoltaic systems at twenty-seven (27) District-owned sites at no cost to the District. Flywheel
Development, LLC’s sole compensation is the future transfer of Solar Renewable Energy Credits
and the District’s agreement to offtake 100% of the electricity generated once systems are
operational.
My administration is available to discuss any questions you may have regarding the proposed
contract. In order to facilitate a response to any questions you may have, please contact Delano
Hunter, Director, Department of General Services (“DGS”), or have your staff contact Dr. Jacque
McDonald, Associate Director and Chief Procurement Officer of Contracts and Procurement,
DGS, at (202) 727-2800.
I look forward to the Council’s prompt and favorable action on the enclosed resolutions.
Sincerely,
Muriel Bowser

(G) The goods or services to be provided, the methods of delivering goods or services, and
any significant program changes reflected in the proposed contract:
If approved, the Contract will authorize the Contractor to provide turn-key solar system
development, including design, construction, interconnection, operation, maintenance,
community solar program operations, and PPA administration for the purpose of deploying
renewable energy to combat climate change, creating innovation, and realizing long-term
cost savings. The Department will purchase all electricity generated by the systems on an
on-going basis. Ultimately, the Department’s goal is to both reduce its energy consumption
from existing traditional energy sources and to lower its overall energy costs.
The Department entered into a Letter Contract with Flywheel Development, LLC, executed
on June 26, 2026, which granted a Notice to Proceed authorizing the immediate
commencement of early‑stage activities necessary to satisfy federal construction‑start
requirements for solar energy projects. This Letter Contract is effective for a period not to
exceed 120 days from its execution by the Contracting Officer and will expire no later than
October 24, 2026.
(H) The selection process, including the number of offerors, the evaluation criteria, and
the evaluation results, including price, technical or quality, and past performance
components:
1 – Request for Qualification (“RFQ”) Solicitation Background:
On August 14, 2020, the Department issued the RFQ to solicit Statements of Qualifications
(“SOQs”) from qualified on-site solar electric power (“Photovoltaic” or “PV”) Project
Developers (the “Offerors”) who showed interest in the Development of Solar Power
Generation System Projects for various facilities within the District’s real estate portfolio.
The pre-proposal conference was held at 2:00 p.m. EST on Monday, August 24, 2020, via
Department of General Services 3924 Minnesota Avenue, NE, Washington D.C. 20019

Council Contract Summary
Page 4 of 10
a Web-x webinar. The proposal submission deadline was set for Wednesday, September
23, 2020, by 2:00 P.M. EST. The RFQ was posted on the DGS website, and email
notifications were sent to potential CBE firms identified through market research as local
companies capable of providing the required services. In addition, an email with the web
site link was sent to the Department of Small and Local Business Development (“DSLBD”)
Opportunities Team to forward to all CBE firms. The Department received a total of (16)
SQLs in response to the RFQ.
SQL Evaluation:
Proposals were examined to determine whether they met all the requirements of the RFQ.
Three (3) of the sixteen Offerors, as failed to provide the required DSLBD CBE
certification and were subsequently deemed non-responsive and removed from further
consideration and evaluation. The proposals from the remaining thirteen (13) Offerors were
then scored on a scale of zero (0) to one-hundred twelve (112) points. The one-hundred
twelve (112) points include (100) points for the technical criteria and up to (12) points
based on the Offeror’s status as a CBE.
Certified Business Enterprise Preference Points:
The SQL was an SBE set-aside procurement, the Department confirmed that each Offeror
possessed a current SBE certification with DSLBD. Thus, up-to an additional twelve (12)
preference points were available for each Offeror based on the points associated with each
category of certification.
Contracting Officer’s Independent Evaluation:
The Department’s Contracting Officer independently scored and reviewed the Offerors.
The Contracting Officer also reviewed the evaluation process followed by the Panel, their
notes and scoresheets, their final consensus technical evaluation, ultimately determining
the Panel’s technical evaluation and proposed scores were fair and reasonable.
Contract Award:
In concurrence with the Panel’s consensus, the Contracting Officer determined that the
SOQs presented by ten (10) Offerors with 70+ evaluated points met the criteria established
in the RFQ and each Offeror’s SOQ provided sufficient evidence of the team’s ability to
perform services efficiently and in accordance with the established requirements. The
Contracting Officer determined it was in the best interest, and most advantageous to the
District to award the proposed Basic Ordering Agreement (“BOA”) Contracts to ten firms.
Department of General Services 3924 Minnesota Avenue, NE, Washington D.C. 20019

Council Contract Summary
Page 5 of 10
2 – Request for Power Purchase Agreement Proposal (“RFPPAP”) Process:
On February 18, 2025, the Department issued the RFPPAP-2 to all ten (10) of the pre-
qualified Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) holders for the development of solar power
generation systems to provide services for Bundle-2. The pre-proposal conference was
held on February 26, 2025, at 2:00 p.m. EST via TEAMS webinar conference. The site
visits to 27 locations were scheduled throughout a six (6) day period starting on March 4,
2025 through March 11, 2025. There were five (5) addenda issued to this RFPPAP.
Technical Evaluation Process:
Each Offeror’s technical proposal was independently evaluated by a Technical Evaluation
Panel (“TEP” or “Panel”) consisting of three (3) DGS staff members. Proposals were
evaluated by the TEP using the criteria as set forth in the RFPPAP. After the TEP members
completed their individual evaluations, the Panel met to develop a consensus technical
score for each Offeror. In developing the consensus score, the Panel discussed the details
of each of the proposals considering the evaluation factors and sub-factors. Then, as a
group, the Panel completed a technical evaluation of each Offeror with respect to each sub-
factor for evaluation. The TEP assigned each sub-factor one of the 6 ratings above and
divided the points available for each factor among the sub-factors in that category. The
TEP met on April 21, 2025 to develop the consensus technical score and the supporting
written narrative.
Independent Evaluation of the Contracting Officer:
The Contracting Officer of the Goods and Services Contracts and Procurement Division
within the Department diligently examined each proposal, conducting an independent
evaluation. This comprehensive review encompassed the entire evaluation process
conducted by the Panel, including their meticulous notes, scoresheets, and the culmination
of their final consensus technical evaluation. Based on this analysis, the Contracting
Officer concluded that the Panel’s scores and technical evaluation of the proposed Offerors
were fair and reasonable.
Although the Contracting Officer’s independent evaluation aligned with the Panel’s
findings, the Contracting Officer determined that the final award will be based on her
independent evaluation scores and the accompanying award summary. This decision aims
to ensure a fair and balanced assessment, taking into account the nuances and merits of
each proposal.
CBE Preference Points:
CBE preference points were not applied under this RFPPAP because the Offerors had
already received CBE preference points during the earlier Request for Qualifications
Department of General Services 3924 Minnesota Avenue, NE, Washington D.C. 20019

Council Contract Summary
Page 6 of 10
(“RFQ”) process. The RFQ, which was used to establish the Basic Ordering Agreements
(“BOAs”), was based solely on qualifications. As such, CBE points were factored into the
evaluation and award of the BOAs, and duplicating those points during this RFPPAP would
not be appropriate.
Price Points:
The pricing component was worth up to (20) points as outlined in the RFPPAP. Offerors
were assigned price points on a sliding scale, with the lowest proposed price receiving all
the available points and the remaining proposals receiving a portion of the available points
relative to their position in the range established by highest and lowest price offers.
Contract Award:
After reviewing the evaluation Panel’s consensus technical scoring, conducting an
independent assessment in evaluating the responsive Offeror, reviewing the underlying
proposal and pricing, the Contracting Officer determined that the Contractor was the
highest ranked Offeror. In addition, the Contracting Officer determined that the Contractor
is responsible, and that the Contractor’s proposed pricing for Bundle-2 – which will be
referenced as Bundle-5 moving forward under the PPA – is fair and reasonable.

Memorandum
To: Delano Hunter
Director
From: Antoinette Hudson Beckham
Agency Fiscal Officer
Reference: Flywheel Development LLC
Proposed Contract No. DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C PPA-26-01
Umbrella Solar Photovoltaic System Power Purchase Agreement – Bundle-5
Date: June 25, 2026
Subject: Fiscal Sufficiency Review
The proposed Umbrella Solar Photovoltaic System Power Purchase Agreement – Bundle-5
(“PPA”, “Contract”, or “Agreement”), Contract No. DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C PPA-26-01,
between the Department of General Services (the “Department”) and Flywheel Development LLC
(the “Contractor” or the “System Owner”) (collectively, the “Parties) provides, at no upfront cost
to the District, turn-key PV System development, including design, permitting, construction,
interconnection, operation, maintenance, and power purchase agreement administration for
Bundle-2, containing twenty-seven (27) sites, for a 20-year term. The proposed solar PPA replaces
the existing PPA with Flywheel Development LLC. There is no cost for the termination of the
existing solar PPA.
As with the existing solar PPA, the Department is guaranteeing to be the offtaker of 100% of the
electricity produced by the solar energy systems for the 20-year term. In return, the System Owner
is able to benefit from the federal Solar Investment Tax Credit, as well as the Solar Renewable
Energy Credits (“SRECs”) produced by the solar energy systems. A SREC is a market-based
instrument that represents the property rights to the environmental, social, and other non-power
attributes of solar electricity generation. One SREC is created for each megawatt-hour of
electricity generated from the solar energy systems. The System Owner owns and is able to
monetize 100% of the SRECs generated by the solar energy systems in the DC SREC marketplace,
which is the most profitable SREC market in the United States.
In the District, each SREC is currently valued at more than $400. If the Department retained
ownership of the SRECs, the Department would be paying a significantly higher rate for its
electricity consumption. Therefore, the Parties acknowledge and agree that, for all services
performed during the 20-year term, the System Owner’s sole compensation from the Department
Department of General Services 3924 Minnesota Avenue, NE, Washington D.C. 20019

Fiscal Sufficiency Review
Page 2 of 2
shall be the Department’s agreement to off-take 100% of the electricity generated by the Systems
and transfer ownership of all SRECs generated by the Systems to System Owner upon
development, installation, and operation of the Systems. It is understood that the System Owner
shall not be due any additional compensation from the Department for design, pre-installation,
construction, operation, or maintenance services. In no event shall the System Owner be entitled
to receive any additional compensation unless authorized in advance and in writing by a duly
authorized Contracting Officer.
Further, beginning on the Service Commencement dates for each individual System, the solar
electricity price paid by the District for output shall be $0/kWh for the term of the PPA. It should
be noted that the electricity provided pursuant to the PPA is not intended to increase the
Department’s total aggregate electricity purchase. The Department’s other electricity purchase
arrangement (namely, the Department’s Agreement for Electricity Services and Supply
Agreement) has the flexibility to allow for a reduced purchase quantity from that vendor in order
to allow for this consumption without exceeding the aggregate purchase needs.
In my capacity as the Agency Fiscal Officer of the Department, I hereby certify that the Contract,
including all 20 years of its performance period, is consistent with the Department’s operating
budget. In consideration of the $0 obligation offering of the subject PPA agreement, availability
of funding in the Department’s operating budget will not be required through the term of the
20‑year agreement, which ends twenty (20) contract years after the last individual System’s
Service Commencement Date. Funding will also not be needed for the termination of the existing
solar PPA with Flywheel Development LLC.
Pursuant to the authority provided under the District of Columbia Fiscal Year 2026 Local Budget
Act of 2025, effective October 23, 2025 (D.C. Law 26‑51; 72 DCR 9797), and the Consolidated
Appropriations Act, 2026, approved February 23, 2026 (Pub. L. 119‑75; 140 Stat. 173), I further
certify that sufficient appropriations are available to cover any termination fees or other financial
obligations that may become due in Fiscal Year 2026 as a result of early termination of the
Agreement.

Subject: Notice to Proceed & Letter Contract (“Letter Contract”)
Ms. Pitts:
This Letter Contract (“Letter Contract” or “Notice to Proceed”) is issued by the Government of
the District of Columbia, Department of General Services (“DGS”) to Flywheel Development,
LLC (“Contractor” or “System Owner”) pursuant to the Procurement Practices Reform Act (D.C.
Code § 2‑351.01 et seq.), Title 27 of the DCMR, including § 27‑2425 (Letter Contracts), and the
authority granted under D.C. Official Code § 10‑551.01 et seq. In accordance with the
Contractor’s proposal submitted in response to the above‑referenced solicitation for a Power
Purchase Agreement (“PPA”) to develop solar photovoltaic systems at twenty‑seven (27)
District‑owned sites (“Bundle‑5”), this Letter Contract authorizes the immediate commencement
of early‑stage work necessary to meet federal construction‑start requirements for solar energy
projects. Upon execution without modification, this Letter Contract serves as the District’s Notice
to Proceed for the Work described herein and is subject to the following terms:
1. Letter Contract. This is a Letter Contract between the Contractor and the District of
Columbia Government, acting by and through its Department of General Services (“DGS” or the
“Department”), and shall govern our relationship until such time as a final Power Purchase
Agreement (“PPA”) is entered into for the work described in the above referenced solicitation (the
“Definitized Contract”); provided, however, that to the extent an issue is not covered in this Letter
Contract, the Request for Power Purchase Agreement Proposal No. DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-

0001-RFPPAP-02 (“RFPPAP-02”) and the Basic Ordering Agreement Contract No. DCAM-21-
NC-RFQuals-0001C (“BOA Contract”) as negotiated shall govern. Once the Definitized Contract
is signed, this Letter Contract shall automatically terminate and merge into the Definitized
Contract.
2. Scope of Work. As of the date of this Letter Contract, the Department is the owner of all
Premises set forth on Exhibit A. The Contractor is hereby authorized to proceed with the design,
pre-installation and construction services required to develop, operate, and maintain the Systems
on the Premises as contemplated in the RFPPAP-02, the BOA Contract, and the PPA Form of
Contract (Exhibit B). The Contractor will be required to provide all management, personnel, labor,
materials, and equipment necessary. The Contractor shall provide such design, pre-installation,
construction, operation, and maintenance services as are required to properly advance the
development of the Systems pursuant to this Letter Contract. The Contractor shall: (i) develop and
complete detailed Systems designs for each System based on the drawings, specifications and other
documentation that the Department provides; (ii) apply for, pay for, and obtain all necessary
construction and other permits from local authorities and Host Utility, except that the Department
shall obtain easements, leases, licenses, consents, acknowledgments, approvals and other rights
and authorizations from other third parties; (iii) install, and test the Systems on the Sites in
compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, including, but not limited to, the
interconnection of each System to its Site Electrical Systems; and (iv) be responsible for the
operation and maintenance of the Site Electrical Systems up until the respective delivery and
acceptance of each System.
2.1 Limitation on Self‑Performance. The Contractor may self‑perform all work authorized
under Section 2 of this Letter Contract. However, while this Letter Contract remains in effect, the
Contractor shall not self‑perform more than fifty percent (50%) of the overall Scope of Work
anticipated for the Definitized Contract. Upon execution of the Definitized Contract, the
Contractor shall perform the full scope of work defined therein.
3. DGS Authority. Under D.C. Official Code § 10-551.01 et seq., DGS is responsible for the
construction, modernization, and energy performance of District-owned facilities, including the
procurement and installation of renewable-energy systems.

thirty (30) days of execution of this Letter Contract (except when otherwise noted):
a. Copies of the certificates of insurance set forth in Section 5 of this Letter Contract to
the satisfaction of the Department.

4. Compensation. The Department is guaranteeing to be the off taker of 100% of the
electricity produced by the solar energy systems for the 20-year term. In return, the System Owner
is able to benefit from the federal Solar Investment Tax Credit, as well as the Solar Renewable
Energy Credits (“SRECs”) produced by the solar energy systems. A SREC is a market-based
instrument that represents the property rights to the environmental, social, and other non-power
attributes of solar electricity generation. One SREC is created for each megawatt-hour of
electricity generated from the solar energy systems. The System Owner owns and is able to
monetize 100% of the SRECs generated by the solar energy systems on the DC SREC marketplace,
which is the most profitable SREC market in the United States. In the District, each SREC is
Department of General Services 3924 Minnesota Avenue, NE, Washington D.C. 20019

Letter Contract
DCAM-21-NC-RFQ-0001C PPA-26-01
Page 4 of 15
currently valued at more than $400. If the Department retained ownership of the SRECs, the
Department would be paying a significantly higher rate for its electricity consumption. Therefore,
the Parties acknowledge and agree that, for all services performed under this Letter Contract, the
System Owner’s sole compensation from the Department shall be, upon development, installation,
and operation of the Systems, shall be the Department’s agreement to offtake 100% of the
electricity generated by the Systems and the transfer of ownership of all SRECs generated by the
Systems to the System Owner. It is understood that the System Owner shall not be due any
additional compensation from the Department for design, pre-installation, construction, operation,
or maintenance services. In no event shall the System Owner be entitled to receive any additional
compensation unless authorized in advance and in writing by a duly authorized Contracting
Officer.
5. Insurance.
A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS. The Contractor at its sole expense shall procure and
maintain, during the entire period of performance under this contract, the types of
insurance specified below. The Contractor shall submit a Certificate of Insurance to
the Contracting Officer (CO) giving evidence of the required coverage prior to
commencing performance under this contract. In no event shall any work be performed
until the required Certificates of Insurance signed by an authorized representative of
the insurer(s) have been provided to, and accepted by, the CO.
If the Contractor and/or its subcontractors maintain broader coverage and/or higher
limits than the minimums shown below, the District requires and shall be entitled to
the broader coverage and/or the higher limits maintained by the Contractor and
subcontractors.

12. Sexual/Physical Abuse & Molestation - The Contractor shall provide evidence
satisfactory to the CO with respect to the services performed that it carries
$1,000,000 per occurrence limits; $2,000,000 aggregate of affirmative abuse and
molestation liability coverage. Coverage should include physical abuse, such as

mental abuse; any actual, threatened or alleged act; errors, omission or misconduct.
This insurance requirement will be considered met if the general liability insurance
includes an affirmative sexual abuse and molestation endorsement for the required
amounts or through a separate stand-alone sexual abuse and molestation policy with
confirmation there are no exclusions for abuse or assault & battery under the
General Liability. So called “silent” coverage or “shared” limits under a
commercial general liability or professional liability policy will not be acceptable.
Limits may not be shared with other lines of coverage. The applicable policy may
need to be submitted to the Office of Risk Management for compliance review.

UMBRELLA SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM
POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT
This Umbrella Solar Photovoltaic System Power Purchase Agreement Bundle-5 (Contract
No. DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C PPA-26-01) (this “Agreement” or “PPA”) is made and
entered into by and between FLYWHEEL DEVELOPMENT, LLC (“System Owner”), and the
DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, a municipal corporation acting by and through its Department of
General Services (“Host Customer”). Each of System Owner and Host Customer may be referred
to herein as a “Party” and collectively, as the “Parties.”
RECITALS
WHEREAS, Host Customer owns and/or controls certain properties located in the District
of Columbia that use electricity, which properties are described in Exhibit A (the “Premises”);
WHEREAS, System Owner entered into a Basic Ordering Agreement (“BOA”) Contract
No.: DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C on February 28, 2022.
WHEREAS, Host Customer issued a Request for Umbrella Solar Photovoltaic System
Power Purchase Agreement Proposal(s) Solicitation Number: DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C
PPA-26-01, pursuant to the Basic Order Agreement Contract No.: DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-
0001C, as supplemented and amended from time to time (the “RFPPAP”), to solicit proposals for
qualified developers to develop solar photovoltaic electric generating systems to be installed on
each of the Premises (each a “System” and collectively, the “Systems”);
WHEREAS, System Owner submitted a proposal in response to the RFPPAP for System
Owner to design, install, own, operate and maintain the Systems;
WHEREAS, the Systems would satisfy a portion of Host Customer’s electricity
requirements at the Premises, and System Owner desires to sell and Host Customer desires to
purchase all of the Output generated by the Systems under the terms and conditions of this
Agreement;
WHEREAS, Host Customer is willing, under the terms and conditions of this Agreement,
to provide System Owner with access to, and the right to occupy a portion of each of the Premises
for the purpose of having System Owner design, install, operate, and maintain the Systems;
WHEREAS, System Owner and Host Customer agree that System Owner will obtain and
retain all Environmental Credits and all Financial Incentives and Tax Benefits associated with the
installation, ownership, operation and Output of the Systems under Flywheel Development, LLC;
WHEREAS, Any and all work performed pursuant to the Umbrella Solar Photovoltaic
System Power Purchase Agreement – Bundle-5 (the “PPA”) shall be governed by the terms and
conditions of the PPA and the BOA.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the agreements and covenants hereinafter set
forth, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby
acknowledged, the Parties hereby covenant and agree as follows:

ARTICLE II
TERM
2.1 Term
The term of this Agreement (the “Term”) is inclusive of all individual systems
(“System(s)”) to be installed pursuant to this Agreement, and shall commence on the Effective
Date. Each individual System shall have its own Service Commencement Date, beginning at the
completion of the Installation Period, which shall last no more than three (3) years after the
Effective Date, and shall be in full force and effect for twenty (20) Contract Years after the
individual System’s Service Commencement Date. This Agreement shall continue in full force
and effect until the date that is twenty (20) Contract Years following the Service Commencement
Date of the last individual System under this Agreement that is successfully installed, tested, and
ready to deliver Output or the expiration of the Installation Period, whichever comes first, unless
terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement. At the expiration of the
Term herein, unless otherwise agreed between the Parties, the System Owner shall remove the
System, at System Owner’s expense, and without damage to Host Customer’s property.
2.1.1 In the event that the installation, operation, maintenance, repair, or removal of the
System(s) causes damage to the roof or any other part of the Site, the System Owner shall, at its
sole cost and expense, promptly repair or restore the roof and any affected areas to their original
condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted. Such repairs or restoration shall be performed in a
timely and workmanlike manner in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and industry
standards. The System Owner shall indemnify and hold harmless the Host Customer from any
claims, liabilities, or expenses arising from such damage, except to the extent caused by the Host
Customer’s negligence or willful misconduct.
2.1.2 If a Site does not host a PV installation within three (3) years of the Effective Date
due to unforeseen conditions, it shall be considered a Termination of that Site only. However, since
the System Owner would not have furnished the PV system in this instance, the System Owner
shall not be entitled to recover any costs through the Termination or claims process.
